source.title: FADE: Why Bad Descriptions Happen to Good Features
source.authors: Bruno Puri; Aakriti Jain; Elena Golimblevskaia; Patrick Kahardipraja; Thomas Wiegand; W. Samek; S. Lapuschkin

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates feature purity and reports examples of neurons responding to multiple distinct patterns. It uses a different measurement framework from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The study reports Purity results, which it interprets as indicating whether strong feature activations are exclusive to a described concept; lower Purity can indicate responses to unrelated concepts. Other metrics and examples without a reported outcome bearing on polysemanticity are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Mainly a framework for scoring feature descriptions, so most Purity numbers measure how well a description fits, not polysemanticity. Two results bear on the claim: a manual inspection finding high polysemanticity in Gemma-2-2b layer 12 neurons (V2), and Llama neurons that score well on simulation but near zero on Purity (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The main conclusion is that single-metric evaluation (e.g. simulation-based) gives incomplete or misleading descriptions, and that a four-metric framework (FADE) exposes different failure modes. Describing SAE features is harder (lower Clarity) even though they score higher on Purity, read as more monosemantic. Larger explainer LLMs, more examples and more prompt shots improve descriptions. High polysemanticity in Gemma-2-2b layer 12 is a secondary observation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses its FADE framework—natural-data activations, LLM ratings, Purity and other alignment metrics, and feature steering—to evaluate feature descriptions. It does not reproduce the original sources' method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported Purity varies by Gemma-2-2b layer, SAE size, feature type, and description method. In the feature 5183 example, the assessed description also changes the reported Purity.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features have higher average Purity than Gemma-2-2b MLP neurons, which the authors read as SAE features being more monosemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse autoencoder features are more monosemantic than the model's own MLP neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger SAEs (65K vs 16K) do not give better description alignment; the authors attribute this to finer-grained concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider SAE dictionaries split concepts more finely, making each feature harder to describe.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: The study evaluates selected features rather than estimating the share of polysemantic neurons across models. It relies on LLM-generated descriptions and LLM ratings, and the authors note possible evaluator and dataset biases. Numerical uncertainty estimates for the reported table values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported metrics and comparisons are omitted where they do not directly measure Purity or the presence of mixed activation patterns. Descriptive examples without a reported outcome relevant to the claim are also omitted.

untested.parts: No share or prevalence of polysemantic neurons; only manual inspection of 50 neurons in one layer of one model.
No test of superposition as the cause.
No test of initialization, regularization or training noise.
No change of the model's activation function, architecture or regularization, and no performance trade-off.
No systematic test of whether mixtures are misread single features. One anecdotal neuron cannot bear on how rare unrelated mixtures are.

missing.what: Across sampled Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct neurons, many with high simulation scores have low Purity. The top 10% by simulation score have worse Purity than the average neuron.
A separate row for the manual inspection of 50 randomly sampled layer-12 Gemma-2-2b neurons, which found high polysemanticity.

record.verdict_notes: Purity is average precision of activations against LLM-rated concept presence. It is lowered both by polysemantic features and by poor descriptions, so on its own it is not a polysemanticity rate. Most rows compare the study's own method or pipeline settings and are unlinked. The relation is borderline; this could be T4.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates selected Gemma-2-2b features in four layers, not a broad share of neurons across language models. It does not establish the prevalence of polysemantic neurons across models or transformer layers generally.
Whether superposition or capacity pressure causes polysemanticity.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.

The study compares selected MLP-neuron and SAE-feature results and SAE sizes, but does not test activation functions, regularization, modern convnets, or whether polysemanticity can be reduced without a large performance loss.
The study gives a specific Llama neuron example, not a systematic prevalence estimate of genuinely unrelated mixtures across models.
The study reports differences among metrics and descriptions, but does not compare outcomes across different activation-range cutoffs.

tranche.reason: Different method (FADE description metrics) applied in new settings, with results bearing on V2 (layer-12 polysemanticity) and V7 (neuron 5183, Figure 3). T3 fits better than the reader's T2, because the method is not aimed at the polysemanticity question.

source_check.notes: Gemma-2-2b 'features' are MLP neurons (Figure 4 caption, Section 4.1, Table 11). Purity scores a description, not a unit. The text doesn't say whether the 50 manually inspected features were all from layer 12. R17's note reverses the names point: the heatmap lacks some names that Transluce's description lists, though it also shows unlisted similar names.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct L19 feature 5183: Transluce (Choi et al.) description has near-zero Purity (Transluce score 0.77). MaxAct* description ('is') has 'significantly higher Purity' (no number given). Authors call the feature clearly polysemantic: names, 'is' in specific contexts, coding patterns.
statements.problem: Gives neuron 5183 'near-zero Purity' as if it were a property of the neuron. In FADE, Purity scores a description, and the near-zero value belongs to Transluce's description only.

statements.correction: On SAEs, FADE reports only that Gemma Scope SAE features have higher Purity than Gemma-2 neurons, which the authors read as greater monosemanticity, and that larger SAEs (65K vs 16K) are harder to describe. They hypothesise finer-grained concept decomposition. Keep the 'non-basis directions are more monosemantic' theme and drop the absorption/hedging theme.
statements.problem: The 'why' text is right, but the covers tag 'SAE latents become polysemantic through absorption, hedging and co-occurrence' has no basis in the text. FADE never discusses absorption, hedging or co-occurrence.
